When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index 0/10 (CALM, no crash signal aligned) vs VIX Spike Tier 2/4 (MEDIUM, 60% probability, backwardation active)
A zero Crash Index means no macro or price signals are calling a drawdown event. VIX backwardation means near-term vol contracts are priced at a premium to longer-dated ones: the market is paying up to hedge the next few weeks specifically. These two readings measure different time horizons and different markets. Both are currently correct in their own lane. Trust the backwardation signal for the vol surface view and the Crash Index for the price-level view.
⚠ These two disagree: Regime State score 13 (STABLE, no regime shift) vs Macro Regime TRANSITIONAL at 25% confidence
The quantitative regime model reads stability at score **13**, but the macro regime overlay flags a transitional state at only **25%** confidence. At such low conviction, TRANSITIONAL is a caution flag, not a forecast. The STABLE score is the stronger near-term anchor; the TRANSITIONAL read warns the stability may not hold.
Today's tension
The Crash Index is at zero and price is calm, but internal structure is at peak divergence stress with VIX term structure already inverted.
Bull

Bear
Mother Jaws composite divergence is at its ceiling of **100**, with **19** bearish diverging pairs against only **3** bullish out of **43** tracked. VIX backwardation is active: the options market is pricing near-term vol expansion that has not shown up in index-level price action.
The tell: VIX term structure is the arbiter. If backwardation deepens and skew activates alongside it, the options market will have confirmed what the divergence internals are already signaling. If backwardation collapses without a price event, the zero Crash Index is the right read.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The macro environment is STABLE on the surface and fracturing underneath. The Crash Index is at 0 / 10 and the Regime State scores 13 (STABLE), so the index-level picture has not broken. But the regime bias is MIXED, the Macro Regime is TRANSITIONAL at only 25% confidence, and the Contrarian score at 40 is generating a partial signal only. You are not in a clean trending state.

For positioning, partial accumulate at 40 does not mean full deployment. The 51% of tracked pairs in active divergence, with 19 bearish against 3 bullish, argues against indiscriminate long exposure. The Contrarian signal and the breadth deterioration are actually consistent with each other: fear and internal stress create the partial buy setup, not a clear all-clear. Express the accumulate selectively, in areas where the bearish divergence has already flushed, not across the index.

The main risk is that the STABLE regime label provides false comfort while the internal structure continues to deteriorate. The reading that forces a tactical reversal is VIX skew activation. Right now skew and adaptive signals are both off, keeping the tier at 2 / 4 and probability at 60%. If skew activates, the options market is pricing a directional event, not just generic vol expansion, and the partial accumulate stance becomes untenable.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The Macro Regime is TRANSITIONAL at 25% confidence, which is near the floor of conviction. TRANSITIONAL at this confidence level means the system cannot commit to either a risk-on or risk-off regime with any certainty.

Combined with a MIXED bias and a Regime State score of 13 labeled STABLE, the overall read is: the current regime has not broken, but it has not confirmed its next direction. A 25% confidence TRANSITIONAL call is a warning that the STABLE label could be challenged, not a forecast that a shift is imminent.

Keep gross exposure in check and prefer positions with defined risk over open-ended directional bets. The regime will clarify as the macro bias resolves out of MIXED toward either a bullish or bearish lean.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Internal market structure is at maximum composite stress. Divergence, here, means two assets that historically move together have started moving apart in price.

The composite zone is ELEVATED at 51% of 43 pairs in active divergence, with a net bearish bias of 16 (19 bearish pairs versus 3 bullish). The Mother Jaws score is at 100, its ceiling.

Correlation drift, the second dimension, measures how much the statistical relationship between two assets has shifted: a pair moving from near-zero correlation to +0.85 is now moving in near-lockstep. A pair drifting from -0.02 to -0.92 has flipped into near-perfect opposition.

Semiconductors versus the broad market (SMH/SPY) have seen their correlation jump from +0.23 to +0.85 while their price paths separate: they are tracking directionally but the magnitude of the move is skewed heavily to one side. NVDA versus AMD is the sharpest break, at -0.92 correlation: two names that used to be near-uncorrelated are now moving in near-perfect opposition.

Copper versus gold (HG/GC) at +0.81 from +0.20 reflects a bifurcation between cyclical and safe-haven demand within commodities. With 19 pairs in bearish divergence, the stress is diffuse and not isolated to one sector.

Asia · Europe · US · Crypto 24/7 — lead-lag detection
Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

The five-day tape shows sharp dispersion across regions. The Nasdaq (NDX) is up +7.1% while the Dow (DJI) has returned only +2.5%, confirming this US move is concentrated in large-cap tech and not distributed across the market.

In Asia, the Hang Seng (HSI) is up +3.2% while Korea's KOSPI (KS11) is down -7.4%. Korea is a proxy for semiconductor and export demand.

Its underperformance against a rallying NDX is the same fracture visible in the SMH/SPY and NVDA/AMD divergence pairs. Europe is holding with the DAX (GDAXI) at +2.5%, but the Swiss Market Index (SSMI) at -0.3% reflects some defensive rotation within European equities.

Crypto is a net drag: BTC at -0.9% and ETH at -2.5% over five days show that risk appetite is not rotating into speculative assets alongside the equity rally. The KS11 versus NDX spread is the sharpest cross-region signal today: the US tech rally is not being confirmed by the global semiconductor supply chain.

AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

Price is calm but the vol surface is not dismissing risk: the Crash Index is at 0 / 10 while VIX backwardation is active and the spike probability sits at 60%. The Crash Index tracks price-level and macro signals for a drawdown event, and none are aligned.

The VIX Spike Detector is reading the options term structure, where backwardation means near-term vol contracts trade at a premium to longer-dated ones: participants are paying up specifically to hedge the near-term window. Skew and adaptive signals are both off, which is why the tier holds at 2 / 4 and not higher.

This is a coherent state, not a contradiction: price is calm while the vol surface prices a near-term expansion risk. The signal to watch is skew activation.

If it fires alongside backwardation, the options market is pricing a directional move, the Crash Index becomes the lagging indicator, and the regime read needs to be revisited.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 0/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
